Paper · 21 Feb 2024

Molecular assembly indices of mineral heteropolyanions

Hazen, Burns, Cleaves, Downs, Krivovichev, Wong · J. R. Soc. Interface 21:20230632

In a sentence

Some mineral building units score above the assembly-index threshold proposed for life.

In plain words

Assembly theory says molecules needing 15 or more joining steps, found in many copies, are a sign of life. This team calculated the score for clusters of atoms that form in water and build some minerals. The most complex, in the rare minerals ewingite and ilmajokite, scored 21, so a high score alone cannot mean life.

Technical detail

Heteropolyanions range from assembly index 2 (H2CO3, Si(OH)4) to 21 (ewingite, ilmajokite). Reply by Walker, Mathis, Marshall and Cronin (J. R. Soc. Interface 21:20240367, 2024): the ~15 threshold comes from experimentally measured covalent organic molecules, while these indices are theoretical, from crystal structures of charged units not isolable in solution. Counter-reply: Hazen et al., 21:20240622.

What we take from it

Planned test

A direct challenge to assembly index as a biosignature; task #7 tests it against a size-only classifier.

Source checked against its DOI. Read the original.
